requirements.statement: In the opening run, 'Save and continue' on 'What are you importing?' goes to 'Main import reason', and 'Main import reason' goes on to 'Commodity details': the reason for import is asked before the numbers of animals and packages.
requirements.why: The target design asks origin, what you are importing, the reason for import and then commodity details, in that order, and the owner's 9 October ruling counts question order as look and feel the prototype decides.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p3-019, repo-frontend-p3-020 and repo-tests-p8-007: the animals frontend and the tests repo now walk origin, 'What are you importing?', 'Main import reason', 'Commodity details'. The older captures of the same journey still show commodity details before the reason (trace-animals-fit-p1-055, trace-e2e-p14-118), so those traces are behind the repos.

requirements.statement: In the opening run, 'Save and continue' on 'Consignment addresses' goes to 'Contact address for this consignment'. The CPH number page and the permanent address page are not steps of the journey: each is reached only from its row on 'Consignment addresses', and saving it returns there.
requirements.why: The target design's step order has no CPH step: roles and addresses is followed by the contact address, and the CPH number and permanent address are reached from inside roles and addresses.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-066 and repo-frontend-p3-047: the CPH number and permanent address pages are sub-pages 'Save and continue' never lands on, and saving the addresses page opens the contact address picker; repo-tests-p4-025 and repo-tests-p8-039-m1: the CPH page returns to the addresses page and Continue there reaches the contact address. The older captures still walk the addresses page on to the CPH page (trace-animals-fit-p1-061, trace-e2e-p14-108).

requirements.statement: When every section on the overview is already complete, 'Save and continue' on 'Consignment addresses' returns to the overview.
requirements.why: The target design skips the rest of the linear run once nothing is left to answer, so a trader who finishes the addresses last lands on the overview.
requirements.deltaNote: Today 'Save and continue' on the addresses page always offers the next page that applies, the contact address picker (repo-frontend-p1-064, repo-frontend-p3-047), whatever the rest of the notification holds.

requirements.statement: A new notification's opening run takes 'Save and continue' from page to page through every question that applies, in the journey's order, without stopping at the overview; the overview is reached by 'Save and return to overview', by 'Cancel and return to overview' or by the notification's own root address.
requirements.why: The target design sends each saved step to the next step in a fixed order. The real journey already does this for a new notification.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p3-074 and repo-tests-p8-013: the opening run carries a new notification from the origin page through every question to its review page in one pass; repo-frontend-p3-108: the overview is reached by 'Save and return to overview' or by the notification's root address.

requirements.statement: 'Save and continue' on the contact address page at the end of the opening run always goes to the review page, even when the notification is incomplete; the review page then names what is outstanding.
requirements.why: In the target design the review is an ordinary step after the contact address, and completeness is enforced only by the overview's statuses and the review page's submit.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p3-079 and repo-tests-p8-040: saving the contact address page of an incomplete notification ends on the notification view, which names what is outstanding in a 'There is a problem' summary reading 'Complete main import reason' and 'Complete consignment addresses'. The review section's own readiness gate is still in the set's flow (repo-frontend-p1-053) and is set aside for the run in c-205.

requirements.statement: A page opened from a task on the overview returns to the overview when it is saved rather than carrying the trader on through the rest of the journey. The service tells such a page apart by where it already records the trader as having come from.
requirements.why: Every overview task in the target design returns to the overview when saved, and the owner's 9 October ruling confirms it. Each page the real journey chains on to has its own row on the overview, so nothing becomes unreachable.
requirements.deltaNote: Today 'Save and continue' always offers the next page in journey order, whatever the page was opened from: a task opened from its overview row carries only the overview as where it came from and still walks on (repo-tests-p8-044, repo-tests-p8-045, repo-frontend-p1-064, repo-frontend-p3-076). 'Save and return to overview' already returns to the overview (repo-tests-p8-147), and the older captures show the earlier behaviour of chaining through a section before returning (trace-animals-fit-p1-059 to trace-animals-fit-p1-062).

requirements.statement: A journey page's Back link goes to the page the trader pressed 'Save and continue' on, to the overview when the page was opened from the overview, to the review page when it was opened from a Change link there whether or not the notification is being amended, and to the overview when nothing says where the trader came from or when it names a place the journey does not have. A page shown again after a refused save still goes back to the page 'Save and continue' was pressed on.
requirements.why: The target design builds every journey page's Back link from the context it was opened in, and the real journey now does the same.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-226 and repo-tests-p8-057: Back now goes to one of five places — the page 'Save and continue' was pressed on, the overview when the trader came from the overview, the review when they came from a Change link (amending or not), and the overview as the fallback; repo-frontend-p1-227: a refused save keeps Back on the page it was pressed on. The older capture still shows Back going to the overview in change mode (trace-animals-fit-p1-083).

requirements.statement: 'Save and return to overview' saves the page and takes the trader to the notification's overview rather than to the next page of the journey. The button submits the service's own exit=hub form field.
requirements.why: The target design treats it as a save that leaves the linear flow. The real journey already does this; form field names are architecture, which the prototype does not decide.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p4-136 and repo-frontend-p3-108: 'Save and return to overview' commits what the trader typed and lands on the overview rather than the next page; trace-animals-fit-p1-050: the button submits exit=hub.

requirements.statement: 'Cancel and return to overview' is a link to the overview that leaves the page without saving what was typed, and it is always available, whatever the page still has unanswered.
requirements.why: The target design's cancel control is a plain link to the overview, and the data specification makes cancel always allowed whatever is unfilled. The real journey already does this.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p4-135: 'Cancel and return to overview' discards what the trader typed and lands on the overview, and repo-frontend-p3-060: it is a link that follows the two save buttons with no checks of its own.

requirements.statement: Every page the overview links to ends with a primary 'Save and continue' button, a secondary 'Save and return to overview' button and a 'Cancel and return to overview' link, in that order, with the two buttons in one button group above the link.
requirements.why: This is the target design's default page ending, and the DR1 rule (b) judgement gives exactly the overview-linked pages these three controls. The real journey already does this.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p3-060, repo-tests-p4-134 and repo-tests-p8-061: a page offering all three controls shows 'Save and continue', then 'Save and return to overview' as the form's last button, then the 'Cancel and return to overview' link below the group.

requirements.statement: The contact address page's return controls read 'Save and return to hub' and 'Cancel and return to hub'.
requirements.why: The target design words the contact address page's return controls with 'hub'. The prototype wins over the frontend's own rule that 'hub' never appears to users, which is not a DR1 judgement.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p3-106 and repo-tests-p4-167: the contact address page words its return controls its own way, and the suite recognises a hub-worded pair ('Save and return to hub' with 'Cancel and return to hub') beside the overview-worded one. The older captures show every page, the contact address page included, reading 'overview' (trace-animals-fit-p1-050, trace-e2e-p14-088).

requirements.statement: While a notification is being amended, the party pickers, the CPH number page and the permanent address page show a primary 'Save and return' button that goes to the review page and a secondary 'Save and continue' button, and no link-styled 'Save and return to overview'. The buttons submit the service's own form fields.
requirements.why: DR1 rule (b) judged where return-to-overview controls go and keeps the hub control off these pages, while the amend-only 'Save and return' and 'Save and continue', which DR1 never judged, follow the target design's amend ending.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a page outside the task-row journey ends with its primary button alone and offers no 'Save and return to overview' (repo-frontend-p3-061, trace-animals-fit-p1-051, trace-animals-fit-p1-052), and an amendment ends every page with exactly the controls it shows on a draft (repo-plantsfrontend-p12-088).

requirements.statement: On every page that offers both, 'Save and continue' and 'Save and return to overview' make exactly the same checks, with no page an exception. A page whose answers all pass saves them, and 'Save and return to overview' then shows the notification's overview. A page with an answer that is missing or does not pass its own rule keeps the trader on the page, shows an error for each such answer, and shows back everything they entered. The answers checked are the page's own hard stops together with any the data specification marks mandatory to proceed; an answer that is only mandatory to submit can still be left blank on either button.
requirements.why: The owner's 26 October ruling adopts the business analyst's expected behaviour: both save buttons behave the same way, upload documents included, and what the trader typed is kept. The data specification says the same.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p4-125 to repo-tests-p4-131: 'Save and return to overview' now makes the same checks as 'Save and continue' on the main import reason, arrival details, commodity details, transporter list and commodity selection pages, refusing each with the page's own errors and leaving its row 'To do'; repo-tests-p4-132 and repo-frontend-p3-028: a page with only mandatory-to-submit answers outstanding, such as additional details, is still accepted on either button. The earlier evidence that the two buttons differed is ruling-sam-2026-10-26-p1-001 and trace-e2e-p13-113.

requirements.statement: Pages inside a notification (the overview, the question pages and the review page) show a status strip above the caption: a blue 'Draft' tag, or the notification's own status, followed by the notification reference in bold, a GBN-AG-<two-digit year>-<six characters> reference minted by the backend when the notification is created. The strip shows from the first request on the origin page and never on the dashboard. The shared strip is not changed in place: a page that needs a different header switches the shared strip off and draws its own header in the set's template.
requirements.why: The target design shows the status and reference on every journey page, with 'Draft' when the notification has no other status. The real journey already does this, and the 9 October afternoon ruling keeps the shared strip as it is.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p4-138 and repo-tests-p4-141: the strip shows a blue 'Draft' tag and the notification's reference from the first request and stays on the overview and every task page; repo-frontend-p1-152: the reference is GBN-AG-YY-XXXXXX in Crockford base32; repo-tests-p4-137: the dashboard carries none. Today the declaration also carries the strip (trace-e2e-p13-010).

requirements.statement: Starting a new notification creates a fresh, empty notification with its own reference and opens its origin page; the trader's other drafts, submitted notifications, templates and address book are kept.
requirements.why: The target design clears the journey's answers when a notification is started but keeps everything else. The real service already creates a new record for each start.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p3-011 and trace-e2e-p13-003: 'Start a new notification' creates a notification with its own reference and redirects to its origin page.

requirements.statement: Opening any page of a notification directly sends the trader to its origin page when the notification holds no answer the trader entered; the origin page itself, the create path and the amend, cancel-amend, copy and delete actions are exempt, and the redirect is logged once with the notification's id and the path that was asked for.
requirements.why: Real notifications are server records anyone signed in can reach by URL, which the prototype (one notification per browser session) cannot express: the entry guard is a real persistence constraint that overrides the prototype.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-094 and repo-frontend-p1-094-m1: every path under a notification is guarded except the create path, the four action slugs and the origin page, the overview among the guarded ones; repo-frontend-p1-095 and repo-tests-p8-050: a notification with no answer the trader entered is sent to its origin page.

requirements.statement: Every page needs a signed-in session: a signed-out trader who opens any page is sent to the service's /auth/sign-in with the page they asked for kept in a 'redirect' parameter, and after signing in returns to that page with its saved answers intact, or to the dashboard when none was asked for. A redirect is followed only when it is a relative path on the same service, and it is used once.
requirements.why: Authentication is a real constraint the prototype cannot express, so it overrides the prototype.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p1-042: a signed-out request to a notification page goes to /auth/sign-in with the path in a redirect parameter and returns to it after signing in; repo-tests-p4-166 and repo-frontend-p3-005: the overview, a question page and check your answers each need a signed-in trader and authorisation is enforced even in stub mode.

requirements.statement: A page opened from the review page returns to the review page when it is saved, and keeps that context through its own in-page actions (add, remove, upload) until it does; 'Save and return to overview' still goes to the overview first.
requirements.why: The target design returns a page reached from the review to the review, with the overview taking precedence over the review, and the prototype wins by default on where a saved page goes.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a page opened from a Change link walks on through the rest of the journey instead of returning to the review: origin reaches the commodity selection page and additional details reaches arrival details (repo-tests-p4-116), and the review is reached only once every later page has been saved (repo-tests-p4-118, repo-tests-p4-121, repo-frontend-p3-084). The context already survives the page's own add, remove and upload round trips (repo-tests-p4-123, repo-frontend-p3-081).

requirements.statement: Every journey page is a server-rendered form: a successful save is a full-page POST answered by a redirect to the next page, each save stores the notification as a draft, and every option list arrives in the page rather than from a browser call to another service.
requirements.why: The target design posts each page and redirects, persisting a draft each time, with every list rendered by the server. The real journey already works this way.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p1-054: a save is a POST to the page answered by a 302 to the next page; repo-frontend-p3-058: each page's answers are posted by one POST form; trace-e2e-p14-121: a notification walked to the declaration is stored as DRAFT; trace-e2e-p13-111: the browser talks only to the frontend.

requirements.statement: A page refuses a save only for its own hard stops; every other answer can be left blank to proceed, and completeness is enforced by the overview's statuses and the review page's submit. For example, a blank transporter and an empty transit countries list are allowed, a reason's follow-up question is required once that reason is chosen, the number of animals is required, and documents are optional unless the trader has started one.
requirements.why: The target design separates what blocks a page from what blocks submission, and the data specification does the same by marking an answer optional, mandatory to proceed or mandatory to submit. The real journey already keeps that separation.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p8-138 and repo-tests-p8-046: the transporter list and the transit countries page both save through unfilled; repo-frontend-p3-026 and repo-frontend-p3-075: the identification details and accompanying documents pages carry on with nothing entered; repo-tests-p4-132: additional details is accepted with both questions blank and its row stays 'To do'.

requirements.statement: On 'Arrival details', in the live-animals and germinal products sets, a save is refused only when the means of transport is missing; the arrival date, port of entry, transport identification and transport document reference can be left blank to proceed. Plants' arrival details keeps its own rules.
requirements.why: The target design makes the means of transport the arrival page's only hard stop, because it decides whether transit countries apply. The 9 October afternoon ruling makes arrival details' own rules animals only.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the arrival details page refuses a date that names no real day as well as a missing means of transport, on either save button (repo-tests-p4-126, repo-tests-p4-127, repo-tests-p8-079), and the obligation model marks the arrival date, the port of entry, the means of transport, the transport identification and the transport document reference all mandatory (repo-frontend-p1-127, repo-frontend-p1-128, repo-frontend-p1-133).

requirements.statement: On commodity details, a save is refused when a line that asks for a number of packages has none.
requirements.why: The target design makes the number of packages a hard stop on that page alongside the number of animals.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a line's number of packages is asked only when its commodity code is on the package-count list and is optional there (repo-frontend-p1-158, repo-tests-p4-027); the number of animals is already refused when blank (repo-tests-p4-129).

requirements.statement: The transit countries step, and its row on the overview, apply only when the means of transport is rail or road; choosing any other means skips the step, takes the row off the overview and deletes any saved transit countries. Transit countries are optional to proceed.
requirements.why: The target design adds the transit countries step only for rail or road. The real journey already does this.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p4-005, repo-tests-p4-006 and repo-frontend-p3-033: the transit countries step and its overview row appear only for rail or road; repo-tests-p4-008 and repo-tests-p4-009: changing the means to one that does not ask for them takes the row off the overview and wipes the saved countries; repo-frontend-p1-136: they are never compulsory.

requirements.statement: The animal identification step follows commodity details only when at least one chosen species has identifiers of its own; a consignment with none never reaches the identification page, and a commodity with none gets no panel on it.
requirements.why: The target design adds the identification step only when a selected species has identifier fields. The real journey already does this.

requirements.statement: The additional details step applies to every live-animals consignment because it always asks what the animals are certified for; its unweaned animals question appears only when a commodity line is one that triggers it, such as cattle.
requirements.why: The target design adds the additional details page whenever it would ask the certification purpose or the unweaned question, and live animals are always asked the purpose. The real journey already does this.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p4-014 and repo-frontend-p1-150: the certified-for question is always asked; repo-tests-p4-015 and repo-frontend-p1-160: the unweaned question shows only once a triggering commodity line exists.

requirements.statement: The CPH number applies when any commodity line's commodity code is one the data specification requires it for, and is out of scope otherwise; for cats, dogs and ferrets each animal's permanent address is asked in place of a CPH number.
requirements.why: The data specification decides which commodities a conditional rule covers, and the owner's 11 November ruling makes its allow-list the shape the service holds, with how the list is held in code the frontend's own call. The target design brings the CPH number in by commodity code and asks a cat's permanent address in its place.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-159 and repo-frontend-p1-194: the CPH number is asked when any commodity line's code is on a seventeen-code allow-list and is out of scope otherwise, which is the shape the 11 November ruling called for; repo-frontend-p1-170 and repo-frontend-p1-196: the three species under 01061900 are asked for a permanent address instead; repo-tests-p4-018 and repo-tests-p8-068: a cats-only consignment shows no CPH row.

requirements.statement: Each reason for import brings in only its own follow-up questions, revealed on the same page: the purpose for internal market; the exit port and destination country for transit; the destination country for transhipment or onward travel; the exit date and port of exit for temporary admission of horses. Changing the reason deletes the follow-up answers that are out of scope for the new reason.
requirements.why: The target design requires a reason's follow-ups once that reason is chosen and walks each branch this way. The real journey already scopes them like this.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-144 to repo-frontend-p1-147: the purpose, destination country, port of exit and exit date are each in scope only for their own reason and are purged when the reason changes; repo-tests-p4-030 to repo-tests-p4-032 prove the reveals and the wipe.

requirements.statement: Only the transporter details that match the chosen transporter type are kept: switching between commercial and private deletes the other type's details.
requirements.why: Keeping one consistent transporter record is a real persistence constraint the prototype cannot express. The real journey already does this.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-130 and repo-tests-p4-038: switching the transporter type drops the other type's stored record.

requirements.statement: An answer to a question that is out of scope is not shown, checked or saved, and any stored value is cleared in the same save; when one field of a collection entry leaves scope only that field is cleared.
requirements.why: The real service must not store answers the notification no longer needs: a real persistence and validation constraint that holds whatever the prototype shows.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-178: a gate that swaps an answer's scope drops the stored answer when the gate answer flips; repo-tests-p4-016 and repo-tests-p4-009 prove it for the unweaned question and the transited countries, and repo-plantsfrontend-p12-055 for plants' arrival status.

requirements.statement: A notification's arrival date counts as complete only when it falls between 7 days in the past and 6 months ahead.
requirements.why: The target design holds the arrival details task back outside that window. The real journey already applies the same window.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p4-062, repo-tests-p4-063 and repo-tests-p8-074: the arrival date must fall between seven days in the past and six months ahead, and a saved date that falls out of the window puts the row back to 'To do'.

requirements.statement: Each journey page carries the caption of the part of the notification it belongs to, immediately above its heading: 'About the consignment' (origin, what are you importing, animal identification, main import reason), 'Description of the goods' (commodity details), 'Commodity details' (additional details), 'Transport and arrival' (arrival details, transporter), 'Movement' (transit countries), 'Add a new transporter' (the add-a-transporter pages), 'Documents' (accompanying documents), 'Addresses' (consignment addresses, CPH number, permanent address) and 'Dashboard' (the set's dashboard). The overview, the contact address page, the review page, the declaration and the confirmation carry none, and nor do the delete-notification and cancel-amend pages, which interrupt the journey rather than belong to a section.
requirements.why: The target design's pages carry these captions, and the owner's 17 November ruling words the addresses section 'Addresses'. The real journey already captions them this way.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-105 to repo-frontend-p1-113: the nine caption sections and the pages in each; repo-frontend-p1-116-m1: the review page, the declaration, the confirmation and the contact address page carry none, and repo-frontend-p3-089: the overview is exempt. The addresses, CPH number and permanent address pages now read 'Addresses' (repo-frontend-p1-109), which the older capture shows as 'Consignment parties' (trace-animals-fit-p1-069).

requirements.statement: Every new or changed piece of user-facing text has a Welsh version, the English and Welsh copy keep the same shape, and a machine-drafted Welsh string does not reach users without Welsh Language Standards sign-off.
requirements.why: The real service is bilingual, a real constraint the English-only prototype cannot express.

requirements.statement: The animals frontend's journey structure holds: the obligation model decides what applies and whether it is mandatory, the journey flow decides the page order and the sections, task rows decide grouping on the overview, each answer is claimed by exactly one page, and the obligation model holds no display copy.
requirements.why: These are the real frontend's recorded rules on how scope, order and grouping are kept apart; every flow change in this area lands through them.

requirements.statement: The animals frontend refuses to start when the journey is not fully configured — a seam left unwired, a journey cookie unregistered, an obligation collected by no page or by two, an obligation carrying display wording, or an obligation id holding a path metacharacter — and the platform's limits hold: scope rules are code, asking the journey flow anything before it is configured raises rather than answering, a page's gate opens when one of its answers is in scope, and a collection entry's position is not a durable identifier.
requirements.why: These are real constraints of the platform every flow change runs on.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-013, repo-frontend-p1-014 and repo-frontend-p1-022: the set refuses to mount on an unwired seam or an unregistered cookie and refuses to answer before the journey flow is configured; repo-frontend-p1-016 to repo-frontend-p1-019: the boot checks on obligation ownership, display keys and ids; repo-frontend-p1-177: a document's instance id is a session-scoped counter value.

requirements.statement: Every page this programme touches passes an accessibility check with no serious or critical violation of WCAG 2.0 A and AA, WCAG 2.1 A and AA or WCAG 2.2 AA, on first render and in its error state, and no page overflows sideways at a 360 by 740 phone viewport or a 1280 by 720 desktop viewport.

A page with no errors shows no summary.

requirements.why: These are gaps in the target evidence; nothing in them says what to build differently.

requirements.statement: What today's traces, suites and repos do not show is recorded, not built: backend calls behind the browser, real identity-provider sign-in, 404 and error pages, no-JavaScript country and port selects in the end-to-end traces, copy as new, cancelling an amendment from the dashboard, where the overview and cancel controls lead from a page opened in change mode, which commodity codes make the CPH number, package-count and unweaned questions appear, how far ahead an arrival date may be, the port-of-entry search's wording and announcements, the no-results wording of either search box, the means-of-transport prompt, a transporter being added inside a whole-journey walk, the look of any journey page other than the origin page, what the Address book, Manage account and Log out navigation items lead to, what a journey page does when the stub address book or reference data cannot be reached, which caption each plants journey page shows under a cross-page test, amending or copying a plants notification, and any heading, copy or validation error on the pages the k6 performance suite drives.
requirements.why: These are gaps in the evidence of today's behaviour; each is weighed where its page is built.

requirements.statement: The suites' fixture data and driving mechanics are test scaffolding, not requirements: the stub sign-in routes and organisation ids, the fresh-organisation trick, the seeded notification stages and the pages a seeded draft posts to, the canned transporters, document files and address-book records, the named parties and country, species and port constants, the field names a seeder posts, the k6 blank-field answers, select defaults, skipped search boxes, sample draft id and endpoint tags, and the Playwright projects, timeouts, retries and video settings each suite runs with.
requirements.why: They describe how the suites drive the service, not what a trader sees; they change only as the journeys they drive change.

requirements.statement: Journey pages keep today's URL paths: the live-animals set at /live-animals, a notification's overview at /live-animals/notifications/{reference} with no slug, a new notification created at /live-animals/notifications, and each page at /live-animals/notifications/{reference}/{slug} with today's slugs (origin, commodities, consignment-details, commodities/identification, import-reason, additional-details, port-of-entry, transit-countries, transporters, accompanying-documents, addresses, cph-number, permanent-address, the five party pickers, consignment/contact/select, notification-view, declaration, confirmation). The prototype's flat paths are not copied, and every flow change is specified and tested by the page, heading and destination it reaches, not by a literal path.

The target design likewise gives germinal products no additional details page.

The guard reads the category each set records when it creates the draft, and treats a notification with no recorded category as live animals, so only the live-animals set opens one.

The reframed notification list stays at the live-animals set root, so the suite's list request does not move.

Plants keeps its own step order, and its rulings ledger records that the opening run ends on check your answers.

Animals-only data (species, animal identification, CPH, transit countries) is never mirrored into plants.

Every page in the flow is either captioned or listed as deliberately bare, each page files under exactly one caption section, and no caption string goes unused. The Welsh captions are machine-drafted and do not ship to users without Welsh Language Standards sign-off.

requirements.why: These are the plants frontend's recorded structure and boot checks; every plants flow change in this area lands through them, as live animals' do, and each set keeps owning its own pages.

requirements.statement: The behaviours the plants rulings ledger parks are not built by this programme: users, sign-in models, agents and delegation; internal-user login; bulk upload, reusing a previous consignment and importing from existing documents; plant-operator registration; regulator, inspector and analyst screens, captures or exports; list maintenance, risk classification and spot-check scheduling; document uploads; lawful basis, privacy notice and retention; refinements from the pre-2021 scheme and the Northern Ireland and Republic of Ireland services; and a meaning for 'sustainable'.
requirements.why: The plants ledger parks each of these until policy or a plants source supplies what is missing, and the goal brings plants in only where it shares a page or behaviour with the animals sets. The ledger itself is no longer in this area's working set, so the parked list is recorded here and the ledger is read where it now sits.

requirements.statement: The plants frontend's high-risk plants set mounts as its own plugin at /high-risk-plants, registering one flat route table assembled from its feature route modules: the notification list at the set base, the create and start paths, the task-list hub, each journey page as a GET and POST pair at its own slug, the three party pickers and their edit pages, and the delete-notification and cancel-amend actions. Its route extensions, the entry guard among them, are sandboxed to that plugin, so another set's routes never run its guards, and the guard runs before every route handler in the set.
requirements.why: This is the plants shell that every mirrored change lands in. It already exists, and the programme keeps plants' architecture as it is, with each set owning its own pages.

requirements.statement: Out of scope: a plants eligibility checker ('Is my consignment high-risk?') or a before-you-start page ahead of the plants journey's first page. The plants journey starts on its own commodity type question.
requirements.why: No source asks for one: the target design has no such page for plants, no ruling asks for it, and the afternoon ruling has plants keep its own questions and step order, with the opening run starting on commodity type.

requirements.statement: Every journey page works fully without JavaScript, and CSS and JavaScript only enhance a page that already works: every state change is a form post, every search or filter is a form with a submitting button that keeps the term the trader typed, and nothing a trader needs is shown only by script. Journey behaviour is built from GOV.UK Frontend first, then the accepted government components (the accessible autocomplete over a native select, and the Ministry of Justice date picker and sub navigation); no increment writes custom JavaScript to copy the prototype, the Ministry of Justice Modal dialog and Copy button are not used, and any other component needs design's case. A prototype behaviour that needs JavaScript no accepted component gives is built in its no-JavaScript version, with the JavaScript-only part its own increment in the waiting-on-design theme, one per design question, changing plants too where the row does.
requirements.why: The 9 October afternoon ruling sets the toolbox and graceful-degradation rule for every page. Today's journey pages already use GOV.UK Frontend with the Ministry of Justice date picker and the accessible autocomplete, and render on the server.

requirements.statement: In every set, readiness works like this: a task row whose question does not apply reads 'Not applicable' and owes nothing; a row with no mandatory part reads 'Optional' while untouched and then 'In progress' or 'Complete'; a row whose stored answers no longer pass its own pages' rules reads 'To do' however complete the engine counts it; a row's link opens the first of its pages whose gate passes and falls back to the row's first page; a card on the review page shows one broken-answer message; the rows roll up into readiness for check your answers; and the overview's 'Review and submit' button reaches the review page whatever is still owed. A row is held back only by the answers a later page is enforced to have — the country of origin and at least one commodity line — and the page that asks for the earliest missing one is offered instead.
requirements.why: The target design enforces completeness through the overview's statuses and the review page, which is how the real journey already works; the step-order and return changes in this area rely on it.

requirements.statement: The live-animals obligation model's scope and mandatory rules for the journey's shared answers are these: the country of origin, whether a region-of-origin code is required, the reason for import, the arrival date at the port, the port of entry, the means of transport, the transport identification, the transport document reference, the five consignment parties, the contact address and what the animals are certified for are always asked and mandatory; the country-of-origin subdivision code and the trader's internal reference are always in scope and optional; the region-of-origin code is always in scope and switches from optional to mandatory when the trader says a code is required, keeping its stored value when the answer changes; the transporter type is always mandatory while the commercial and private transporter records are mutually exclusive and each in scope only for its own type; the transited countries are asked of rail and road consignments only and are never compulsory; a conditional answer whose in-scope decision names no mandate counts as mandatory; a notification must hold at least one commodity line; and the notification's reference number is system-populated, mandatory and asked by no page.
requirements.why: These are today's obligation rules for the journey's shared answers; nothing in the target design or the rulings changes them, and the step-order and return changes must not either.

requirements.statement: How the DR1 parity build run was organised is not a requirement: its union of runs A and C, increment numbering and provenance blocks, corpus profiles and report locations, frozen source backlogs and the commits its findings were authored against, build target and verification ladder, the address-space and disputed-band holds and their parked branches, and the build order and code touch points of its own increments.
requirements.why: The DR1 notes count only for DR1 judgements on a difference the real frontend and Design Release 2.1 clash on; these notes record how that earlier programme was run, which judges no difference. This is the same judgement as req-1734, which now carries it: both say that DR1's own records build nothing on their own, and this id stays so that it still resolves.

requirements.statement: How the data specification lays out each field, in eight headings: field name, type, conditions or values, the level it applies at, source, whether it is mandatory, an example, and the journeys it impacts.
requirements.why: Weighed here and left out: it describes how the source is written, not anything a user or another system can observe. This is the same judgement as req-2211, which now carries it; this id stays so that it still resolves.

requirements.statement: An answer the data specification marks mandatory to proceed must be given before its page can be left by either save button. An answer marked mandatory to submit can be left blank while the notification is being filled in and is needed only before it is submitted. An answer marked optional can be left blank throughout. An answer marked conditional is needed only while its stated condition holds, judged at the level the answer applies at.
requirements.why: The data specification's Mandatory column is the policy on which answers are a page's hard stop and which only hold back submission. The owner's 10 November ruling drops the obligation model row that would have recorded it, because the service already tells a hard stop from a submission check and refuses a half-filled document group, so nothing is built for this on its own.
requirements.deltaNote: Today an in-scope obligation is marked mandatory or optional only and a conditional gate that names no mandate counts as mandatory (repo-frontend-p1-137), and a mandatory answer is enforced by the review page's submit rather than on its own page: additional details is accepted with both questions blank and its row stays 'To do' (repo-tests-p4-132).

requirements.statement: A group of answers the data specification marks all-or-nothing can be left blank as a whole, and once any answer in the group is given every answer in it is needed: the page refuses either save button with an error for each answer still missing from that group, and the group's row on the overview counts as complete only when all of the group is given or none of it is.
requirements.why: The data specification marks some answers as a group that must be filled in together, so a half-filled group is never stored or submitted. The owner's 10 November ruling drops the obligation model row that would have recorded it, because the service already refuses a half-filled document group, so nothing is built for this on its own.
requirements.deltaNote: Today no all-or-nothing rule across a notification's scalar answers exists; the nearest rules are the document and collection ones, which make all four of a document's details mandatory within that document (repo-frontend-p1-174) and hold a row back from reading complete while a required collection is empty (repo-frontend-p1-089).

requirements.statement: Whatever level an answer applies at, an answer the trader gives is checked before it is saved: the right format, within the length allowed, and one of the list's entries where the answer has a list. An answer that fails is refused with its own error and the trader's own entry is shown back.
requirements.why: The data specification makes validity a rule of every answer, whatever its level, and the real service cannot store a value that does not fit its field. The journey already works this way.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p4-050, repo-tests-p4-084 and repo-tests-p4-155: an answer that is too long or too large is refused with its own message, whatever level it applies at; repo-tests-p4-127: a refused page shows the trader's own entries back.

requirements.statement: An answer the data specification sets out is asked in both the live-animals and the germinal-products sets unless the specification marks it for one of them, and where both sets ask it but allow different values each set offers its own list.
requirements.why: The data specification covers both sets in one page and marks the exceptions, so the germinal set's questions are the live-animals set's except where the specification says otherwise. The germinal set does not exist yet, so every one of its answers comes from this rule.

requirements.statement: The data specification page's own bookkeeping is not built: its page version and title, its statement that the fields are agreed, the eight headings each field is specified under, the two spellings of the commodity level, and its change log's columns, its unnamed authors, its missing reasons for the six de-scopings and its silence on the address block.

requirements.statement: A journey page is told where the trader came from by the trail the service writes into the page's own address: the places already saved, newest last, named in the service's own words (the dashboard, the overview, the Import Notification Service and the review page). requirements.statement: A trader who opens a journey page before the answers it needs have been given is offered the page that asks for the earliest missing one instead, with the page they asked for and every missing answer recorded, and the page they came from kept so Back returns to it. conflicts.about: How far the checks on both save buttons reach: every mandatory answer on the page, or only the answers the page already refuses, the consignment addresses page and the party pickers included

'Exactly the same checks as Save and continue' keeps each page's existing hard stops and adds nothing, while 'an error message for each answer that is missing or not valid' would refuse a page whenever any mandatory answer is blank, which would stop a trader leaving a part-filled page at all and undo the leave-and-come-back model the overview's statuses and the review page's submit enforce. Both readings are the top-ranked source's own words, so precedence ranks neither, and the data specification's split between mandatory to proceed and mandatory to submit sits below it. Built to the default until it is answered. The consignment addresses page and the party pickers were raised separately as the same decision read against those pages, and are recorded here rather than twice: on the first reading they do not change, and on the second the ruling reverses the blank pick and the empty section that Design Release 2.1 designs and that the 9 October afternoon ruling gave plants' pickers.

conflicts.outcome: Unsettled, and the two readings build different services. The 9 October ruling kept ?change=1 and added no marker, and on its plain reading the trail that the save and continue work has since merged into both frontends comes out and the review context goes back to ?change=1. The other reading is that how a service remembers where a trader came from is its own architecture, which the ruling described rather than decided, and that the 10 November ruling deferred the return links to exactly that merged work; the trail then stays and the return and Back rules are specified against it. Precedence ranks neither, because the later ruling defers to the work that built the trail while the earlier one names the flag, so the question goes to the owner. Nothing about where a saved page or a Back link goes turns on the answer: req-1615, req-1616, req-1639 and req-1917 state those destinations without naming the mechanism.
conflicts.question: Does the journey keep the trail it now writes into each page's address as the way it remembers where a trader came from, or come off it and go back to the ?change=1 flag with no trail?
conflicts.default: The trail stays, in both frontends. A page's address carries the places already saved, newest last, in the service's own names; the review context is the review page's own place on that trail instead of ?change=1; and no page of the merged save and continue work is reverted. New work specifies the return and Back rules by where the trader came from rather than by the query that records it.

conflicts.about: Where a page opened from a Change link on the review page goes when it is saved

positions.says: On look and feel the prototype wins by default over what the real services do today.
A section page returns to the review page when it continues and was reached from the review.
Save and continue on a page opened by a Change link goes on to the next journey page rather than straight back to the review.
Pressing Save and continue from a page opened by a Change link walks every later journey page in turn and ends on the review.
Saving the accompanying documents page opened on the review trail opens the consignment addresses page.

conflicts.outcome: Design Release 2.1 outranks what the real frontend does today and no DR1 judgement or real constraint covers it: a page opened from the review page returns to the review page when it is saved. Walking the rest of the journey from a Change link is set aside. repo-frontend-p3-084 is not set aside, because it also records that the review offers a 'Change document 1' link that opens the accompanying documents page, which stays true.

conflicts.about: Which environments every link, redirect and form hand-over between services has to work in, and how that is proved

positions.says: Links between services must work in CDP, in the local Docker stack and in the CI Docker stack, all three.
The ruling names CDP as a whole and no environment within it, such as dev, test or production.
The ruling does not say how working links in all three environments are to be proved, so no check or evidence is named.
The Import Notification Service's type-question URL is built from the configured base URL with any trailing slash removed.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling cannot be met as written in every part of the target: it names CDP as a whole, and the programme deploys to some CDP environments and not others, while the two Docker stacks have an end-to-end suite that can prove a link and CDP has none. Two readings build different things — one proves every link in every CDP environment, the other proves what each environment can prove and takes the rest from one shared configuration — and nothing ranks them, so the question goes to the owner with a default that says what each part gets.
conflicts.question: Which CDP environments must every link, redirect and form hand-over between services be proved to work in, and what counts as proof there?
conflicts.default: Each link, redirect and form hand-over resolves from the calling service's own configuration with no hard-coded host or port. It is proved in the local Docker stack and the continuous-integration Docker stack by the end-to-end suite walking the hand-over, and in CDP dev and test by one walk of the journey on the deployed services. CDP perf, pre-production and production take the same configuration and get no proof in this programme.
